The High Light at Ling Hill (1858). The Low Light next to it was removed c.1890 and is a separate tower.

Two towers in 1879-87: Smeaton's high light (1776, pulled down 1895) and the 1852 low light. The main light was Smeaton's, and Wikidata has no item for it. Q26365310 is its 1895 replacement. Q26630126 (low light, 1852) did stand then; use it only if a tower of the station is good enough.
A Lincolnshire village (observer's place). Candidates matched on the word 'Great' only.
The 1840 tower. St Edmund's chapel light is the 1665 forerunner.
An inland Norfolk village, an observer's place.
High light (1791), the main light. The low light was pulled down in 1883 and has no candidate.
High light, rebuilt 1874 on the same site. The low light on the beach was separate.

The candidates are the Harwich and Dovercourt leading lights, on the Essex side 2-3 km away. They are different lights from Landguard Point (Suffolk side).
Two towers, both lit in 1879-87. The Upper is the main light; the Lower (Q26323604) is the second tower.

In 1879-86 the light was Wyatt's 1792 tower. Q26543919 is the 1904 tower, built because the shore had moved. Q3739774 is from 1961. The 1792 tower's base survives right next to the 1904 tower, so on a chart the 1904 position is off by only a few tens of metres.
Belle Tout (1832) was the Beachy Head light until 1902. Q15197902 is the 1902 tower below the cliff.
One item for the station's three towers. It is the only candidate (no Findlay row).
Gätke's observing station, not a lighthouse row. No candidates.

Printed 'Allonby L.H.', but I know of no lighthouse at Allonby, and there is no Findlay row or candidate. Check the 1881 page: it may be a misprint for a nearby Solway light (Silloth, Hartley) or the observer's home.
Rebuilt 1866 on the same site.

Findlay 1879 'AIR POINT' falls on the 1776 Talacre tower (0.15 km). But I believe this tower was replaced by an offshore pile light in 1844, which became a lightship c.1883. There is no Findlay 1887 row, yet 'Air, L.H.' is reported to 1887. Check which structure the keeper was at.

The reports say Breakwater, so I picked the 1873 breakwater-head lighthouse. The Findlay rows 'Holyhead' fall on the Mail Pier light (Q15224748, 0.14 km), so the Findlay match may be to the wrong harbour light. Q5887001 is the breakwater as a structure.
A fog-signal station, not a light. The candidates match only the word 'Stack'/'Station'.
Findlay gives no position. Matched on name and the 1870 inception. Little Castle Head (Q28824545) is its separate partner light.
As I understand it, the present St Ann's Head lighthouse (1841) is the old front/low light, and the high light went out in 1910.
The old rear/high light (out 1910, tower still standing) has no candidate. Q7586969 is the low light.
Single row for 1884-87, when both lights were still lit. Q7586969 is the only item. It is the low light, about 100-200 m from the high light.
The West/low tower (out of use c.1900), which is the westerly item at -3.5567.
The East/high tower, still in service.
Findlay 1879's longitude (-3.05) looks misprinted; the 1887 figure fits. East Usk is from 1893.
None of the candidates is the Avon/Avonmouth light: Portishead Point is 1931, Black Nore 1894, Charston Rock is up-channel.
High lighthouse, the main light. The Low (wooden, on legs) is the front light of the pair.
The item's inception (1879) is the original tower. That tower was replaced c.1974 after a cliff fall, a little inland. Check whether the item's coordinates are for the new tower.

Findlay's 'Bideford' (lon -4.20/-4.208) fits the Braunton Burrows high and low lights (1820-1957) on the west side of the estuary. Instow (front/rear) is on the east side, 1.7-2.1 km away, and Crow Point is from 1954. None of the candidates is the Braunton light.
The Old Light (1820). North and South lights came in 1897.
The fog-gun battery on the west side is separate from the Old Light. Q17536768 is a fair proxy position if needed.
The main/upper light. Trevose also had a low light in the early years.
The 'Scilly' light was St Agnes until 1911.
The 1858 tower, encased and heightened 1883-87 on the same rock.
Twin towers, both lit until 1903. One item covers the station.
Douglass tower (1882); reports start in 1884.
In 1886-87 there were High and Low lights (1869). The High is the main light. The present lighthouse (Q2753005) is from 1903-06, on a new site.
High light (1867), the main light. Q5856579 is the low lights on the castle wall; their present form dates from 1911.
The main tower. The Low Light is from c.1890.

Three towers. By 1881-82 only one light was lit, the one still in service (the 1818 item here). The 1779/1781 octagonal tower and the other 1818 tower (labelled 1825) were out of use.

Two stations under one id. Before 1884 the light was on Lighthouse Island (Copeland). The Mew Island light, picked here, was lit in 1884, and the printed 'Copeland (Mew) Island' points to the later years. Q126714836 ('Former light house buildings', 1839) may be the old Lighthouse Island station. Consider splitting by year.

Same single item for both towers. Its coordinates appear to be the East (south) Maiden, which is still lit.

'Lough Swilly' is matched to Fanad (Fannet) Point. Dunree has its own row.
Findlay gives no position. Oyster Island had two towers, and the printed 'N.' suggests the north one. Wikidata has a single item.

notes:
I picked a Wikidata item for 158 of the 183 stations and left 25 null. Most picks are high confidence; I made them from the candidate file and what I know of these lights' histories, without looking anything up in Wikidata.

Things to check:
1. Lights with no item for the 1879-87 tower (null): Spurn (Smeaton's 1776 high light; the 1895 tower replaced it, and the 1852 low light could stand in), Dungeness (1792 tower; the 1904 tower is a few tens of metres away), St Ann's High, Bideford (I think Findlay's position means the Braunton Burrows lights, not Instow), Avonmouth, Landguard Point. South Gare, Calf Rock and Stevns Fyr had no right candidates at all; look those three up in Wikidata directly.
2. Copeland is two stations under one id. Before 1884 the light was on Lighthouse Island; the Mew Island light was lit in 1884. Split it by year; Q126714836 may be the old site.
3. Point of Ayr (Flintshire): the Talacre tower may have been replaced by an offshore pile light (1844) and then a lightship (c.1883), but reports run to 1887. Check what the keeper was at.
4. Holyhead Breakwater: the Findlay rows match the Mail Pier light, not the breakwater-head light the reports name. The Findlay match may be wrong.
5. Twin-tower stations where one Wikidata item covers both towers, so both rows get the same QID and position: Maidens N/S, Eagle Island E/W, Slyne Head N/S, Oyster Island. The towers can be up to about 1 km apart, so get separate coordinates for each if the chart needs them.
6. Printed forms that may be misassigned: 'Longness L.V.' (Langness), 'Tuskar Rock Lt.-ship' (Tuskar), 'Straw Island, S.,' (in Inisheer), 'Allonby L.H.', 'Stornoway (2 Lights)'. Dursey's Findlay 1887 match is the CALF ROCK row.
7. Stations where the light was rebuilt near its old site and the Wikidata coordinates may be the newer tower: Bull Point (rebuilt c.1974), Douglas Head.
8. Findlay positions that look misprinted (1879 vs 1887): West Usk 1879 longitude, Fladda 1879 latitude, Holy Isle 1879 latitude.
9. Main light chosen where the station had two lights: Whitby High, Happisburgh, Orfordness, Lowestoft, South Foreland Upper, Burnham High, Portland High, Hurst High, Pentland Skerries High, Isle of May main, Pladda main. Skellig: the lower light, since the upper went out in 1870. Wicklow: the one tower still lit after 1865.
10. Duplicate candidate rows in the input (e.g. Holyhead Q5887001, Turnberry, Whitby West Pier beacon) suggest positions.py emits one row per coordinate statement. That is harmless, but worth deduplicating.
